+class TestStartupPluginImportErrors:
+    """Exit codes for plugins which fail to load at startup (#993).
+
+    A plugin which cannot be found means pytest was pointed at something which
+    is not there, which is a usage error; a plugin which is found but blows up
+    while importing is a defect in the plugin, reported as an internal error.
+    """
+
+    @pytest.fixture
+    def broken_plugin(self, pytester: Pytester) -> Pytester:
+        pytester.syspathinsert()
+        pytester.makepyfile(myplugin="raise ValueError('plugin is broken')")
+        pytester.makepyfile("def test_foo(): pass")
+        return pytester
+
+    @pytest.fixture
+    def missing_plugin(self, pytester: Pytester) -> Pytester:
+        pytester.syspathinsert()
+        pytester.makepyfile("def test_foo(): pass")
+        return pytester
+
+    def test_missing_via_cmdline(self, missing_plugin: Pytester) -> None:
+        result = missing_plugin.runpytest("-p", "nosuchplugin")
+        assert result.ret == ExitCode.USAGE_ERROR
+        result.stderr.fnmatch_lines(['*Error importing plugin "nosuchplugin"*'])
+
+    def test_missing_via_conftest(self, missing_plugin: Pytester) -> None:
+        missing_plugin.makeconftest("pytest_plugins = ['nosuchplugin']")
+        result = missing_plugin.runpytest()
+        assert result.ret == ExitCode.USAGE_ERROR
+
+    def test_missing_via_env(
+        self, missing_plugin: Pytester, monkeypatch: MonkeyPatch
+    ) -> None:
+        monkeypatch.setenv("PYTEST_PLUGINS", "nosuchplugin")
+        result = missing_plugin.runpytest()
+        assert result.ret == ExitCode.USAGE_ERROR
+
+    def test_broken_via_cmdline(self, broken_plugin: Pytester) -> None:
+        result = broken_plugin.runpytest("-p", "myplugin")
+        assert result.ret == ExitCode.INTERNAL_ERROR
+        result.stderr.fnmatch_lines(
+            [
+                'Error while loading plugin "myplugin".',
+                "*myplugin.py:1: in <module>*",
+                "E*ValueError: plugin is broken",
+            ]
+        )
+
+    def test_broken_via_conftest(self, broken_plugin: Pytester) -> None:
+        broken_plugin.makeconftest("pytest_plugins = ['myplugin']")
+        result = broken_plugin.runpytest()
+        assert result.ret == ExitCode.INTERNAL_ERROR
+
+    def test_broken_via_env(
+        self, broken_plugin: Pytester, monkeypatch: MonkeyPatch
+    ) -> None:
+        monkeypatch.setenv("PYTEST_PLUGINS", "myplugin")
+        result = broken_plugin.runpytest()
+        assert result.ret == ExitCode.INTERNAL_ERROR
+
+    def test_usage_error_passes_through(self, pytester: Pytester) -> None:
+        """A plugin raising UsageError at import keeps its usage-error semantics."""
+        pytester.syspathinsert()
+        pytester.makepyfile(
+            myplugin="import pytest\nraise pytest.UsageError('config trouble')"
+        )
+        result = pytester.runpytest("-p", "myplugin")
+        assert result.ret == ExitCode.USAGE_ERROR
+        result.stderr.fnmatch_lines(["ERROR: config trouble*"])
+
+    def test_broken_via_entry_point(
+        self, pytester: Pytester, monkeypatch: MonkeyPatch
+    ) -> None:
+        monkeypatch.delenv("PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD", raising=False)
+
+        class DummyEntryPoint:
+            name = "myplugin"
+            group = "pytest11"
+
+            def load(self):
+                raise ValueError("plugin is broken")
+
+        class Distribution:
+            version = "1.0"
+            files = ("foo.txt",)
+            metadata = {"name": "foo"}
+            entry_points = (DummyEntryPoint(),)
+
+        monkeypatch.setattr(
+            importlib.metadata, "distributions", lambda: (Distribution(),)

title: fix(rewrite): prevent walrus operator double evaluation in assertions
body:
## Summary

Fixes #14445 — assertion rewriting evaluated walrus operator (`:=`) expressions
multiple times, so an assertion over an expression with side effects reported a
result the test never actually computed.

**Root cause:** the `variables_overwrite` mechanism stored `NamedExpr` AST nodes
and substituted them back into every later read of the target name — in
subsequent assertions, in `_call_reprcompare`'s results tuple, and in
explanation formatting. Each substitution is another evaluation.

**Fix:** remove `variables_overwrite` entirely, and instead

- keep walrus expressions in their natural evaluation position, so left-to-right
  order is the interpreter's, not the rewriter's;
- reference the target variable in explanations rather than re-evaluating it;
- freeze conflicting left operands via `assign()` when a later walrus targets the
  same name, so the explanation reports what that operand actually saw;
- capture BoolOp conditions in stable temps for the explanation path.

The `self.scope` / `_SCOPE_END_MARKER` bookkeeping goes with it: it existed only
to key `variables_overwrite` per scope.

## What is in the diff

Four files, ~160 lines of rewriter change:

| file | |
| --- | --- |
| `src/_pytest/assertion/rewrite.py` | the fix |
| `testing/test_assertrewrite_coverage.py` | +15 matrix cases, all passing |
| `testing/test_assertrewrite.py` | net shrink, see below |
| `changelog/14445.bugfix.rst` | |

### Coverage

The new cases in the matrix cover single evaluation (`compare`, `boolop`,
chained compare) and evaluation order — that an operand evaluated *before* a
later walrus is reported with its pre-assignment value, for compare left
operands, call arguments (positional, keyword and `**`), BinOp left operands and
chained-compare operands.

The three evaluation-order cases @scapalive reported are among them. They are
not regressions from this PR — they fail on `main` too — but they are the same
defect, so they are fixed and covered here rather than deferred.

### Test cull

`TestAssertionRewriteWalrusOperator` is gone. Nine of its twelve `runpytest()`
tests are answered more precisely by the matrix, two moved there (one as
introspection, one as evaluation order), and one stayed in
`test_assertrewrite.py` because it needs two tests in one module to say
anything. `TestIssue14445` keeps the two reproducers from the issue itself.

The composite-chain case is the reason this is a cull and not just tidying: it
passes on `main`, and it passes *because* of the bug. `main` rewrites the walrus
target to an internal temp and substitutes the stored `NamedExpr` into every
later read of the name, including the next statement — so the `assert a is None`
meant to verify the outcome re-runs the walrus and produces the value it is
checking for. Asked through returned values instead of `ret == 0`, `main` fails
that case.

## Review notes

@bluetech — the BoolOp explanation you flagged is fixed on this branch. On

```py

    return True

title: Allow int for max_warnings in TOML
body:

title: Replace string nodeids with a structured NodeId internally
body:
pytest identified every collection-tree node with a plain "::"-joined nodeid string, repeatedly re-parsed (split/partition) at dozens of call sites for cache persistence, terminal/JUnit reporting, and stepwise/ subtests bookkeeping. Introduce a NodeId dataclass (src/_pytest/_nodeid.py) and use it internally as the dict/set key and equality type everywhere a nodeid was previously compared or looked up as a string, while keeping the existing nodeid: str property as a full backward-compatible surface for external plugins.

Function's NodeId also carries structured per-parametrize-call data (ParamId: id/argnames/scope) when built from live collection data, laying groundwork for future scope-aware scheduling (e.g. in pytest-xdist) without committing any consumer to it yet.

@@ -0,0 +1,113 @@
+"""Structured representation of a pytest "nodeid".
+
+A nodeid is represented as a ``::``-separated string, identifying a node in the collection
+tree, e.g. ``path/to/test_file.py::TestClass::test_method[param]``.
+
+The :class:`NodeId` class represents that information in a proper dataclass with the relevant
+parts readily available, avoiding reparsing that information when needed and also making for
+a better type than `str`.
+
+The traditional ``::``-joined string form remains available via ``str(node_id)``.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import dataclasses
+
+
+@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True, kw_only=True)
+class NodeId:
+    """Structured identifier of a node in the collection tree.
+
+    :param path:
+        ``/``-normalized, rootpath-relative filesystem path.  Empty string
+        for the session root.
+    :param names:
+        Ordered ``::``-segment names after the path.
+    :param params:
+        Raw contents inside the outermost ``[...]`` bracket, kept as one
+        opaque string -- traditional string-node ids are often recovered from the outside (for example
+        files), so we cannot recover the actual params and values used to build the parametrization.
+    """
+
+    path: str
+    names: tuple[str, ...] = ()
+    params: str | None = None
+    _str_cache: str | None = dataclasses.field(
+        default=None, init=False, repr=False, compare=False
+    )
+
+    @classmethod
+    def parse(cls, nodeid: str) -> NodeId:
+        """Parse a nodeid string into its path, names, and raw params."""
+        path, sep, tail = nodeid.partition("::")
+        if not sep:
+            # No "::" -- everything is the path.  Never interpret a bracket
+            # here: file paths can legitimately contain "[" (e.g. test[1].py).
+            self = cls(path=path)
+        else:
+            # Peel the params bracket off the tail FIRST.
+            name_part, bracket, param_part = tail.partition("[")
+            names = tuple(name_part.split("::"))
+            params = param_part.removesuffix("]") if bracket else None
+            self = cls(path=path, names=names, params=params)

+A nodeid is a ``::``-separated string identifying a node in the collection
+tree, e.g. ``path/to/test_file.py::TestClass::test_method[param]``.
+
+There are three structured, internal representations of this concept, all
+only ever built from live collection data or from a specific external
+boundary -- so that their fields can always be trusted:
+
+- :class:`CollectionNodeId` -- for a ``Collector`` node (can still have
+  children). ``.child()``/``.leaf()`` build further ids on top of it.
+- :class:`ItemNodeId` -- for an ``Item`` node (a leaf, e.g. a test
+  function). Carries ``params``; has no ``.child()``/``.leaf()`` at all, so

+  function). Carries ``params``; has no ``.child()``/``.leaf()`` at all, so
+  building further collection-tree structure on top of one is a static
+  type error, not just a runtime mistake.

+  code that genuinely needs to accept/hold either kind.

title: fixtures: use a better data structure for storing FixtureDefs
body:
This PR fixes #14942.

### The commits

The 1st and 2nd commits are related internal documentation fixes.

The 3rd commit is a little refactor to encapsulate access to `FixtureManager._arg2fixturedef` to make the next commit clearer.

The 4th commit is main change, I reproduce the commit message below.

The 5th commit adds backward compat for string nodeids in `register_fixture`. I split it from the previous commit to make it easier to review the main change without the ugly compat. I will squash it before merging.

### Description

Previously, FixtureManager stored the registered FixtureDefs in `_arg2fixturedefs` which is

    <fixutre name> -> [FixtureDef]

where the FixtureDefs are ordered by visibility.

There are two inefficiencies with this:
1. When registering a fixture, we need to find the appropriate index to insert in the list. This is done with slow quadratic `is_visibility_more_specific` checks.

   Before 7186cd46553a14bfc1ee0e6e77e5daa6c3882bd4, FixtureDefs were always appended, relying on the collection order, so there was no quadratic issue. But then we added `pytest.register_fixture` which is not guaranteed to be called in collection order.

   This is #14942, introduced in v9.1.0.

2. When looking up FixtureDefs for a node, the entire list needed to be filtered for visibility to the node (`_matchfactories`). With many fixtures registered with the same name (even if completely unrelated), this can be slow.

   This is an old issue.

Change the way we store the FixtureDefs to `_arg2node2fixturedefs`, which is

    <fixture name> -> (Node -> [FixtureDef])

i.e. instead of storing the FixtureDefs for a name in a single big list, store them by the Node under which they are registered.

This fixes (1) since now just need to append to `arg2fixture2nodes[name][node]`.

Fixes (2) since no longer need to filter a big list (scaling with number of fixtures registered with same name). Instead need to look up the FixtureDefs registered for the node and its ancestors (scales with height of the collection tree, which should be OK).

### Performance

Performance numbers with reproducer from https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14942#issuecomment-5454638951 (`NCLASSES=10000 time pytest reproducer.py`):

- This PR: 11.0s
- main: 35.0s
- Commit before 7186cd46553a14bfc1ee0e6e77e5daa6c3882bd4: 16.7s

It's still kinda slow, but a profile shows that's for other preexisting reasons. The improvement over main is due to fixing problem (1), and over before the regression due to fixing problem (2).

### Backward compat

This breaks plugins which directly access `FixtureManager._arg2fixturedefs` (double private :grinning:). From my local corpus (678 plugins), I see it done in these plugins:

- pytest-bdd - Moderately elaborate usage. I will try to send a PR to fix if this is merged.
- pytest-deadfixtures - Just iterates over all FixtureDefs. I will send them a PR if this merged.
- python-pytest

+    )

 # pytest caches rewritten pycs in pycache dirs
@@ -379,7 +387,37 @@ def _read_pyc(
         if not isinstance(co, types.CodeType):
             trace(f"_read_pyc({source}): not a code object")
             return None
+        # A cached pyc can be moved together with the source file (for example
+        # by renaming a package or test directory). In that case the marshaled
+        # code object's ``co_filename`` still points to the old source path.
+        # Fix it in memory the same way importlib does for ordinary pycs: the
+        # cache stays valid, only the in-memory location is corrected.
+        return _fix_code_filename(co, str(source))
+
+
+def _replace_code_filenames(co: types.CodeType, filename: str) -> types.CodeType:
+    """Pure-Python fallback: rebuild the code object tree with *filename*."""
+    return co.replace(
+        co_filename=filename,
+        co_consts=tuple(
+            _replace_code_filenames(c, filename) if isinstance(c, types.CodeType) else c
+            for c in co.co_consts
+        ),
+    )
+
+
+def _fix_code_filename(co: types.CodeType, filename: str) -> types.CodeType:
+    """Point *co* and its nested code objects at *filename*.
+
+    Mirrors what importlib does for every pyc it loads: the cache stays valid,
+    only the in-memory location is corrected.
+    """
+    if co.co_filename == filename:
+        return co
+    if _imp_fix_co_filename is not None:
+        _imp_fix_co_filename(co, filename)  # in place, recursive, C
         return co
+    return _replace_code_filenames(co, filename)

title: Warn when writing or closing a cache file fails
body:
Fixes #15043.

`cache.set()` already warns when opening a cache file fails, but an `OSError` from writing or closing it currently escapes. Move the existing write into the same error handler so these failures also produce `PytestCacheWarning`.

The regression test covers open, write, and close failures. The write and close cases fail before the fix; all three pass afterward. A separate reproduction using a real file-size limit also fails on pytest 9.1.1 and unmodified main, then produces warnings with this fix.

Checks on macOS:

- Full Python 3.13 suite, `tox -e py313 -- -q`: 4,607 passed, 51 skipped, 15 xfailed, 5 xpassed.
- Cache tests on Python 3.12 and 3.13: 68 passed on each.
- `tox -e linting`: passed.

JSON serialization and warning filters keep their existing behavior.

Co-developed by Poorva Barve and Codex.

title: Clarify the relation between marks and keywords
body:
I prompted an agent (Claude Opus 5 in Claude Code) to work through #4569. The
investigation, the commits and this description are its work; I read it and I
am posting it.

---

#4569 asks to revisit the relation between marks and keywords. Mapping what
that relation actually is came first, and it changes the shape of the issue:

**`-k` does not read `item.keywords`, and has not since 2.4.0 (#306).**
`KeywordMatcher.from_item` builds its own name set from the node chain,
`extra_keyword_matches`, the test function's `__dict__` and `iter_markers()`.
`node.keywords` is a separate mapping, fed by different code, read only by
`request.keywords`, `TestReport.keywords` and the terminal's skip folding.

So the two mark-to-keyword hacks from #4564 and #4649 are independent of one
another, and the `# todo: this is a hell of a hack` comment pointing at #4569
sits on the one that does not influence selection at all. That makes most of
#4569 a documentation and coverage problem rather than a refactoring one.

One commit per item:

### Behaviour

* `-k` no longer matches attributes that land in a test function's `__dict__`
  without anyone meaning them as keywords. `-k wrapped` selected every
  `functools.wraps`-decorated test and `-k pytestmark` every directly marked
  one. Private and dunder names are skipped, plus a named set. The legacy
  `test_func.slow = True` idiom keeps working.
* `add_marker` stores a `Mark` in `node.keywords` instead of a
  `MarkDecorator`, matching what collection-time marks store.

### Documentation

* The `-k` help text described the pre-5.4 implementation ("a Python evaluable
  expression"), limited matching to test names and parent classes, and never
  mentioned markers — the thing The-Compiler's comment on #4569 asks for. It
  now lists the real keyword sources and contrasts with `-m`.
* `markers.rst` framed `-k` as name-only and corrected itself only in a
  trailing paragraph; `usage.rst`, which the option reference links to, still
  described eval semantics.
* `KeywordMatcher`, `Function`'s `keywords` parameter, `TestReport.keywords`,
  `Node.keywords` and `FixtureRequest.keywords` docstrings were stale or wrong.
* The `--runslow` and incremental examples use `get_closest_marker` rather than
  `"name" in item.keywords`.

### Tests

Pins `-k` matching marks from module/class/base classes, `-k` ignoring marker
arguments, `-k` seeing a mark added by a conftest collection hook,
`extra_keyword_matches` on an item, and writing into `item.keywords` having no
effect on `-k` or `-m` — despite the 2.3.4 changelog claiming it integrates
with `-m`. Also enables the `-k` half of `test_mark_expressions_no_smear`,
commented out since the marker transfer was removed, and pins that `-m` is
case sensitive.

### Deliberately left open

Whether the `function.__dict__` scan should exist at all is the remaining
design question in #4569. Dropping it means deprecating attribute-marks and
finding another discriminator for the skip folding in `terminal

-select tests based on their names:
+which implements a substring match on the test's *keywords*, instead of the
+exact match on markers that :option:`-m` provides.

@@ -224,10 +225,37 @@ Or to select "http" and "quick" tests:

+A test's own name is only one of its keywords.  The others are:
+
+* the names of the test's parents, usually the file and class it is in
+  (``test_server.py``, ``TestClass``);

+  explicitly added to it or to its parents.

+Marker names being keywords is why ``-k webtest`` selects ``test_send_http``,
+whose name contains no ``webtest`` at all:

+    $ pytest -v -k webtest

title: Bugfix 14412 subtests timing
body:
## Summary

Fixes #14412.

When using `console_output_style="times"` and running subtests, timing information for subtests and the parent test's `PASSED` report could be displayed incorrectly (e.g. `0.000us` or missing).

This occurs because subtests share their parent test's `nodeid`. In `console_output_style="times"`, timing output suppresses subsequent reports for the same `nodeid` once marked as reported, and subtest reports were not handled as distinct progress lines.

### Solution

This PR resolves the issue by:

1. Tracking the current report in `pytest_runtest_logreport` via `self._current_logreport`.
2. Handling `SubtestReport` directly in `_write_progress_information_times()`: when the current report is a `SubtestReport`, its own duration is formatted and returned directly (when `self.showlongtestinfo` is enabled) without modifying `_timing_nodeids_reported`.
3. Retaining `_timing_nodeids_reported` tracking by `nodeid` to ensure teardown timing does not leak into subsequent test lines.
4. Excluding `SubtestReport` instances from the `not_reported` accumulation list, ensuring subtest durations are not counted twice in per-module timing totals.
5. Using `self._current_logreport.location[0]` (with fallback to `all_reports[-1].location[0]`) to ensure accurate module location tracking.

Regression tests have been added to verify subtest timing with and without `xdist`, as well as ensuring slow fixture teardowns do not leak into the next test line.

## Attribution

This pull request was implemented with assistance from AI coding tools (Antigravity), credited via the `Co-authored-by` trailer in the commit history according to pytest's contribution guidelines.

Co-authored-by: Shimon Schwartz (@shimonenator)
Co-authored-by: Antigravity

title: mapping compare - use key-views instead of sets to account for mutating view style mappings (case-insensitive)
body:
## Scope change

This PR originally broadened the `isdict()` dispatch guard from `dict` to `collections.abc.Mapping` for #14461. **That part has since landed** via #14504, which also split the comparison helpers into their own modules. The branch has been reset onto `main` and now carries only the part that is still missing.

## What is left

`_compare_eq_mapping` matched up keys by building plain sets from the two mappings:

```python
set_left = set(left)
set_right = set(right)
common = set_left.intersection(set_right)
```

That discards any key equivalence a mapping defines for itself. A case-insensitive header mapping — `requests.structures.CaseInsensitiveDict` and friends — iterates keys in their original casing, so two mappings with identical content and different casing intersect to nothing, and every key is reported as extra on both sides:

```
Left contains 2 more items:
{'content-type': 0, 'accept': 1}
Right contains 2 more items:
{'Content-Type': 1, 'Accept': 1}
```

The comparison now goes through the key views instead:

```python
keys_left = left.keys()
keys_right = right.keys()
common = keys_left & keys_right
```

Key views are `Set`s whose operations resolve membership through the mapping, so each mapping's own key semantics are preserved:

```
Omitting 1 identical items, use -vv to show
Differing items:
{'Content-Type': 0} != {'Content-Type': 1}
```

Every key the set operations produce remains valid for indexing both sides: `&` only yields keys contained in both mappings, and `-` only yields keys from the side that is then indexed. For plain `dict`s this is the same C-level view operation as before, so there is no cost on the common path.

## Not covered

Multi-value mappings (`multidict.MultiDict` and similar) still lose information, but plain sets were never the cause there — `Mapping.__getitem__` exposes only the first value per key, so duplicate entries are invisible through the interface this function works with. Fixing that needs a different mechanism and is out of scope here.

## Tests

- `test_stdlib_mapping_types` — parametrized over `MappingProxyType`, `ChainMap` and `UserDict`, covering the non-`dict` stdlib mappings that #14504 left untested.
- `test_mapping_with_own_key_equivalence` — a `requests`-style case-insensitive mapping written inline, so no new test dependency. It fails on `main` with the misleading output shown above.

Full suite passes; `pre-commit` including mypy is clean.

title: Mark editable-installed plugins for assertion rewriting
body:
## Problem

`_mark_plugins_for_rewrite()` decides which modules to mark for assertion rewriting by walking the Python files recorded in each plugin distribution's metadata. A PEP 660 editable install doesn't record them — `dist.files` only holds the `__editable__*.pth` shim and the `dist-info` entries — so nothing matches and the plugin never gets marked.

The effect is that assertions inside a plugin stop being rewritten as soon as it is installed with `pip install -e .`, which is the usual way to work on one. With a plugin that asserts in its own helpers:

```python
# myplug/helper.py
def compare(got, want):
    assert got == want
```

```
# pip install .
E       AssertionError: assert {'a': 1, 'b': 2} == {'a': 1, 'b': 3}

# pip install -e .
E       AssertionError
```

## Fix

When a distribution is installed in editable mode and its recorded files yield no rewritable module, fall back to the top-level package of its `pytest11` entry points. Editable mode is read from `direct_url.json` (PEP 610), so regular installs keep taking the existing file-based path untouched.

The `direct_url.json` gate matters. Without it the fallback also fires for distributions that simply record no files, which a number of tests in the suite construct, and 13 of them change behaviour.

## Tests

The new test covers three distributions: an editable one, a regular install from a local directory, and one installed from an index with no `direct_url.json`. Only the editable case fails on `main`.

Fixes #11783

+def _plugin_rewrite_name(module: str) -> str | None:
+    """Return the name to mark so that ``module`` is rewritten.
+
+    This is the outermost package of ``module`` that is not a namespace
+    package: a namespace package can be shared with distributions that have
+    nothing to do with the plugin, and marking it would rewrite those too.
+
+    Names are resolved through ``PathFinder`` because it does not import
+    anything, and the plugin must not be imported before it is marked.
+    """
+    parts = module.split(".")
+    search_path: list[str] | None = None
+    for i, part in enumerate(parts):
+        spec = importlib.machinery.PathFinder.find_spec(part, search_path)
+        if spec is None:

+        if spec.origin is not None or spec.submodule_search_locations is None:
+            return ".".join(parts[: i + 1])
+        search_path = list(spec.submodule_search_locations)

+    if read_text is None:

+    direct_url = read_text("direct_url.json")
+    if not direct_url:
+        return False
+    try:

+    except ValueError:

title: feat(mark): expose `pytest.ParameterSet` in public API (#13431)
body:
### Description

This PR addresses #13431 (part of the public API typing roadmap #7469) by exposing `ParameterSet` in the public `pytest` namespace as the return type of `pytest.param()`.

Currently, developers using `pytest.param` in typed helper functions that return parameter sets receive private import warnings (such as Pyright's `reportPrivateImportUsage`) when importing `ParameterSet` from `_pytest.mark.structures`.

### Summary of Changes

- **Public export**: Exposed `pytest.ParameterSet` in `src/pytest/__init__.py` and included it in `__all__`.
- **Module declaration**: Set `__module__ = "pytest"` on `ParameterSet`.
- **Private constructor**: Refactored `ParameterSet` as a `NamedTuple` subclass with a `__new__` constructor that calls `check_ispytest(_ispytest)` so direct instantiation issues a `PytestDeprecationWarning`, while internal factories (`pytest.param()`, `extract_from()`, etc.) instantiate with `_ispytest=True`.
- **Factory methods**: Marked internal classmethods (`param`, `extract_from`) with `:meta private:` so Sphinx autodoc does not surface them under `pytest.ParameterSet`.
- **Documentation**: Added `pytest.ParameterSet` to `doc/en/reference/reference.rst` under `Objects`, and removed the obsolete entry from `nitpick_ignore` in `doc/en/conf.py`.
- **Changelog**: Added `changelog/13431.improvement.rst`.
- **Tests**: Added comprehensive unit tests in `testing/test_mark.py` verifying public export, `isinstance` checking, deprecation warning on unflagged initialization, and `pickle` serialization.
- **Authors**: Added myself to `AUTHORS`.

Closes #13431.

title: Annotate FixtureRequest.node as Any and document why
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"RonnyPfannschmidt"} -->
_Requested by **Ronny** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_016UJjZXYjfpXuyNsZWbXxvR?thread=cmsg_016UJjZXYjfpXuyNsZWbXxvRMNj5fWEfNZssbDSg3MYPjF)_

🤖 Written by Claude Opus 5.5 via Claude Code for the pytest maintainers; I prompted it, it did the work, I read it.

`FixtureRequest.node` is deliberately not typed as `Node`. See bluetech's reasoning in https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13888#issuecomment-3511168937. Several PRs have tried to add that annotation (#15103, #15226), and it would break typed user code such as `request.node.function` or `request.node.rep_call` under mypy.

This PR:

- adds a source comment above `FixtureRequest.node` that explains the decision and links the reasoning;
- annotates the return as an explicit `-> Any`. Strict pyright reports an unannotated return as `Unknown` (`reportUnknownMemberType` on every `request.node` access). An explicit `Any` fixes that, and mypy treats both forms the same. Suggested by Contrabang in review.

Verified: pyright strict on `request.node.nodeid` / `.function` goes from 6 errors to 0, and `mypy --strict` stays clean.

Refs #13888.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_01FbVKGSuPZFfJpPHTPANBQa

--- /dev/null
+++ b/changelog/13888.misc.rst
@@ -0,0 +1 @@
+:attr:`FixtureRequest.node <pytest.FixtureRequest.node>` is now explicitly annotated as returning ``Any``, so strict pyright no longer reports it as ``Unknown``. The return type stays deliberately broad, see :issue:`13888`.
diff --git a/src/_pytest/fixtures.py b/src/_pytest/fixtures.py
index 20e43f89132..e3d6300b599 100644
--- a/src/_pytest/fixtures.py
+++ b/src/_pytest/fixtures.py
@@ -564,9 +564,18 @@ def fixturenames(self) -> list[str]:
         result.extend(set(self._fixture_defs).difference(result))
         return result
 
+    # The return type is intentionally ``Any``.
+    # The concrete node type depends on the request scope, so the only correct
+    # annotation would be a broad one (``Item | Collector``). That would force
+    # users to ``assert isinstance(...)`` or ``cast`` whenever they know the
+    # actual type (e.g. ``request.node.function`` in a function-scoped
+    # fixture), so we trade type safety for convenience here.
+    # It is spelled out explicitly because pyright in strict mode reports an
+    # unannotated return as ``Unknown`` rather than ``Any``.
+    # See https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13888#issuecomment-3511168937.
     @property
     @abc.abstractmethod
-    def node(self):
+    def node(self) -> Any:
         """Underlying collection node (depends on current request scope)."""
         raise NotImplementedError()

title: tmpdir: hand out numbered dirs from a per-prefix counter
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"RonnyPfannschmidt"} -->
_Requested by **Ronny** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_016UJjZXYjfpXuyNsZWbXxvR?thread=cmsg_016UJjZXYjfpXuyNsZWbXxvRStBm5SmoryYY9KZJ4WBT64)_

🤖 Written by Claude Opus 5.5 via Claude Code for the pytest maintainers; I prompted it, it did the work, I read it.

Closes #15254.

`TempPathFactory.mktemp()` and `tmp_path` used `make_numbered_dir()`, which lists the whole basetemp on every call to find the next free number. basetemp gains entries with every test (two directories and a `*current` symlink per test in the issue's reproducer), so a session does O(N²) work. At N=3000, profiling put 41 of 54 s in `find_prefixed`.

This PR is a simpler alternative to the stat-validated listing cache proposed in the issue. The factory keeps a per-prefix counter (`_next_number`, keyed by the lower-cased prefix):

- `mktemp(numbered=True)`, and through it `tmp_path` and pytester, counts from 0 without listing basetemp. The factory always creates basetemp itself (a fresh `pytest-N`, or a `--basetemp` it has just wiped).
- `mkdir` decides uniqueness. A name it fails on (a directory, file or dangling symlink already there, or a `PermissionError` on Windows for a name still being deleted) is skipped. After 10 failures in a row, basetemp is listed once to jump past the run. After 20, an `OSError` chained to the last error is raised, so a filesystem that reports every name as taken cannot make it loop forever.
- `make_numbered_dir()` and its other callers (the `pytest-of-<user>` session root) are unchanged.

## Behaviour differences

- `mktemp` numbers are no longer "greater than any existing one". Existing names are skipped instead, and the docstring now says so. With a basetemp the factory owns, that only matters for directories something else creates there.
- Numbers never go down. With main, a number freed by the `tmp_path` retention removal could be reused.
- On a case-sensitive filesystem, a foreign `X2` no longer pushes `x` past 2, because `mkdir` decides the collision. Main matched the listing case-insensitively.

Covered by tests: no listing in `mktemp`, unexpected entries (directory, file, dangling symlink), a run of 50 taken names (one listing), overlapping prefixes (`test_a` and `test_a1` both produce `test_a10`), the probing limit, and retries on other `OSError`s.

## Numbers

Reproducer from the issue (`pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider`, noisy cloud box, wall-clock):

| tests | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 1000 | 3.9 s | ~3–4 s |
| 2000 | 10.9 s | ~3.5 s |
| 4000 | 37.3 s | ~7.5 s |

Run time now grows linearly. What remains is mkdir/symlink syscalls.

## Checklist

- [x] Include new tests or update existing tests when applicable.
- [x] Allow maintainers to push and squash when merging my commits.
- [x] Add text like ``closes #XYZW`` to the PR description and/or commits.
- [x] If AI agents were used, they are credited in `Co-authored-by` commit trailers.

reviewComments.body:
pytester calls `mktemp(name, numbered=True)` and `mktemp(f"tmp-{name}", numbered=True)`, with name being the test function name:

https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/blob/431f3e1f5fd70b9b0f8afa2d20a10421542e5c6a/src/_pytest/pytester.py#L699-L699

https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/blob/431f3e1f5fd70b9b0f8afa2d20a10421542e5c6a/src/_pytest/pytester.py#L711

Since the counter is per prefix, and almost every pytester test has a distinct function name, each of them still goes through `seed_from_listing` and lists `basetemp` twice. `basetemp` grows over the session, so pytester-heavy suites (like our own) still pay the quadratic cost.

My point is that we might be missing an opportunity here to speed up pytester, and pytest's test suite as well. One option would be to have pytester skip the listing since it creates its directories through the factory anyway.

title: docs: clarify typing for yield fixtures
body:
### Description
While working with adding types to a codebase of mine and using mypy it was not so trivial (for me at least) that fixtures that are of Generator types, are not to be type annotated like Generators but rather their return types when used in other fixtures. Based on: https://docs.pytest.org/en/stable/how-to/fixtures.html#teardown-cleanup-aka-fixture-finalization, it became more obvious why this is the case, but it was not so easy to find this documentation, and I feel that the typing docs can also have a note for it.

### Changes
Added a typing section about usage of yield based fixtures for other fixtures.

### Relevant issue
No relevant issue, as I see this as small docs "enhancement".

+

+        assert sample_yield_fixture == 38
+
+The test receives the yielded ``int``, not the generator object. See :ref:`How to use fixtures <how-to-fixtures>` for more information about
+``yield`` fixtures and teardown.

<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"RonnyPfannschmidt"} -->
_Requested by **Ronny** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_016UJjZXYjfpXuyNsZWbXxvR?thread=cmsg_016UJjZXYjfpXuyNsZWbXxvRRCzNeBjiFcHjxGCXFjUL8K)_

🤖 Written by Claude Opus 5.5 via Claude Code for the pytest maintainers; I prompted it, it did the work, I read it.

Closes #15242.

The Get Started page told users to run a bare `pip install -U pytest`, which fails with `error: externally-managed-environment` ([PEP 668](https://peps.python.org/pep-0668/)) on current Debian/Ubuntu/Fedora system Pythons.

Changes:

- **Get Started**: says to install into a virtual environment and shows it in three tabs: venv + pip, uv (`uv add --dev pytest`, then `uv run pytest`), and virtualenv. Links to the good-practices section for details and for installing the project under test.
- **Good Integration Practices**: the "Install package with pip" section becomes "Install package in a virtual environment" (old anchor kept via an explicit label). It carries a note on the `externally-managed-environment` error and why not to use `--break-system-packages`. The `pyproject.toml` example gains a `[dependency-groups] dev = ["pytest"]` table, and the install step has the same three tabs (`pip install -e . --group dev` needs pip >= 25.1; `uv sync` installs the `dev` group by default).
- `changelog/15242.doc.rst`.

Built locally with `sphinx-build -n`; tabs render and internal refs resolve. Intersphinx inventories were unreachable from my environment, so the new `packaging:specifications/dependency-groups` doc ref was not verified locally.

- [x] `closes #15242` in the description and commit.
- [x] AI agent credited in `Co-authored-by` trailer.
- [x] Changelog entry added.

+    Uses :mod:`venv` and :doc:`pip <pip:index>`
+    (``pip install --group`` needs pip 25.1 or newer):
+
+    .. code-block:: bash
+
+        python3 -m venv .venv
+        source .venv/bin/activate   # on Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
+        pip install -e . --group dev
+        pytest
+
+.. tab:: uv
 
-    pip install -e .
+    `uv <https://docs.astral.sh/uv/>`__ creates ``.venv``, installs your
+    package in editable mode and installs the ``dev`` group by default:
+
+    .. code-block:: bash
+
+        uv sync
+        uv run pytest
+
+.. tab:: virtualenv
+
+    Same as with :mod:`venv`, but the environment is created by
+    :doc:`virtualenv <virtualenv:index>`:
+
+    .. code-block:: bash
+
+        virtualenv .venv
+        source .venv/bin/activate   # on Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
+        pip install -e . --group dev
+        pytest
 
 which lets you change your source code (both tests and application) and rerun tests at will.
 
+.. _`system-pytest`:
+
+Using pytest from the operating system
+^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
+
+Some projects deliberately use the ``pytest`` provided by the operating system,
+for example to test software that is itself built and packaged by a distribution,
+or where a test suite only needs ``pytest`` to be available as a command.
+In that case install ``pytest`` with the system package manager
+(for example ``apt install python3-pytest`` or ``dnf install python3-pytest``),
+not with ``pip`` into the system Python.
+The version is then the one your distribution ships, which may be older than the latest release.
+
 .. _`test discovery`:
 .. _`Python test discovery`:

reviewComments.body: The getting started page should be "fast". I think it's enough to just show the right way (install to a venv). Maybe the "externally-managed-environment" note can be moved to some other page?
reviewComments.diffHunk:
@@ -9,11 +9,52 @@ Get Started

 ----------------------------------------
 
-1. Run the following command in your command line:
+Install ``pytest`` into a virtual environment, not into the Python installation
+of your operating system.
+Many systems, such as recent Debian, Ubuntu and Fedora releases, refuse a plain

+Do not work around this with ``--break-system-packages``;
+create a virtual environment instead.

reviewComments.body:
I know places which prefer to use pytest itself from the operating system package.

For a public example, I recently saw that PostgreSQL is considering using pytest: https://www.postgresql.org/message-id/DKSSP47Y857Z.1FUU91WMDZWPZ@jeltef.nl
And they rightly don't intend to use a venv, just expect pytest to be available as command.

But, I'm saying this not to change the recommendation, I think the text is fine. Just some subtlety :)

+
+
+
+Improvements in existing functionality
+--------------------------------------

+- `#10745 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/10745>`_: A ``RecursionError`` whose recursion origin cannot be located now shows only the

+  the origin failed outright. Previously the full traceback -- often around a
+  thousand near-identical frames -- was rendered, which was both slow and
+  unreadable. Pass ``--full-trace`` to see every frame.

+- `#10745 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/10745>`_: The line numbers of a module's statements are now computed once per traceback

+  failures raised from large test modules.

When something is dropped, it ends with a note pointing to the element text, which still holds the full report. Previously, very verbose assertion output (e.g. with ``-vv``) produced attributes tens of thousands of characters long, which some XML parsers fail on.
+
+
+- `#12307 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12307>`_: Fixed truncation of long collections (lists, dicts, sets, etc.) in the "message" part of failed assertions (as in ``assert condition, msg``) when using ``-vv``: the message now uses the same unlimited repr as the rest of the assertion output, instead of eliding collection elements with ``...``.
+
+
+- `#12824 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12824>`_: Custom command-line options now fail with a clear error when their implicit
+  destination conflicts with an existing option, avoiding silent overrides of
+  built-in options such as ``-k``.
+
+
+- `#13292 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13292>`_: Fixed a stale rewritten module being used when a test file is modified twice
+  within the same second without changing its size -- the pyc header could only
+  record whole-second timestamps. The cache is now keyed on a hash of the source.
+
+
+- `#14036 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14036>`_: ``__tracebackhide__`` is now respected in ``ExceptionGroup`` tracebacks, both for the group itself and for its sub-exceptions.
+
+
+- `#14189 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14189>`_: Nested usage of :meth:`caplog.filtering <pytest.LogCaptureFixture.filtering>` no longer removes filters early if they were already present.
+
+
+- `#14412 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14412>`_: Fixed incorrect timing information for subtests and parent tests when ``console_output_style="times"``.
+
+
+- `#14445 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14445>`_: Assertion rewriting no longer evaluates walrus operator (``:=``) expressions more than once, which reported results the test never computed when the expression had side effects.
+
+  An operand evaluated before a later walrus is now reported with the value it actually saw, so ``assert value != identity(value := value.lower())`` keeps Python's left-to-right order.
+
+
+- `#14552 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14552>`_: Fixed stale ``co_filename`` values after a test module or directory is moved. Assertion-rewrite caches are reused when the source hash still matches, and in-memory code objects are pointed at the current path.
+
+
+- `#14586 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14586>`_: Negative values passed to ``log_auto_indent`` now correctly fall back to no indentation, matching the documented behavior.
+
+
+- `#14619 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14619>`_: Fixed a crash in ``pytest.mark.parametrize`` when a non-sequence value is passed for a parameter set. It now provides a clear error message during collection.
+
+
+- `#14635 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14635>`_: Fixed fixture resolution failures when specifying multiple test paths on the command line that share common parent directories. Parametrized fixtures defined in a ``conftest.py`` could be silently dropped depending on the order of the specified paths.
+
+
+- `#14637 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14637>`_: Pytest now correctly skips identical trailing characters in assertion text diffs even when the compared strings differ at the beginning.
+
+
+- `#14638 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14638>`_: Top-level options in ``pytest.toml`` and ``.pytest.toml`` files now raise an error instead of being silently ignored when no ``[pytest]`` table is present.
+
+
+- `#14675 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14675>`_: The :confval:`truncation_limit_lines` and :confval:`truncation_limit_chars` configuration options now accept integer values in TOML configuration files, while still accepting strings for backward compatibility.

@@ -31,6 +31,453 @@ with advance notice in the **Deprecations** section of releases.
 
 .. towncrier release notes start
 
+pytest 9.2.0 (2026-10-27)
+=========================
+
+Removals and backward incompatible breaking changes
+---------------------------------------------------
+
+- `#14716 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14716>`_: :option:`-c` now raises a usage error for a path that does not exist, is a directory, or is in a format pytest has no loader for. Such paths were previously either ignored or reported as an unhandled ``FileNotFoundError``.
+
+
+- `#8593 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/8593>`_: The ``indirect``, ``ids`` and ``scope`` arguments of :func:`Metafunc.parametrize() <pytest.Metafunc.parametrize>` -- and therefore of :ref:`@pytest.mark.parametrize <pytest.mark.parametrize ref>` -- are now keyword-only.
+
+  Passing them positionally was a common source of confusing errors, e.g. ``parametrize("arg1", "arg2", [(1, 2)])`` made the argvalues land in ``indirect`` and failed with ``indirect fixture '(1, 2)' doesn't exist``; such mistakes now fail with an understandable ``TypeError``. The type annotations have always declared these arguments as keyword-only.
+
+
+- `#993 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/993>`_: Plugin import failures at startup are now reported and classified instead of escaping as a raw traceback with the accidental exit code ``1``:
+
+  * a plugin that cannot be found -- via ``-p``, ``pytest_plugins`` or ``PYTEST_PLUGINS`` -- exits with :class:`pytest.ExitCode` ``USAGE_ERROR`` (``4``), like a ``conftest.py`` that fails to import;
+  * a plugin that is found but raises while importing -- including a broken ``pytest11`` entry point or a missing plugin dependency -- exits with :class:`pytest.ExitCode` ``INTERNAL_ERROR`` (``3``), with the traceback preserved.
+
+  :func:`pytest.main` now returns these codes instead of raising ``ImportError``. Also fixed an ``IndexError`` from pytest's own internals when the plugin raised an exception with no arguments.
+
+
+
+Deprecations (removal in next major release)
+--------------------------------------------
+
+- `#14742 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14742>`_: The private ``_pytest.python.CallSpec2`` name has been renamed to ``CallSpec``.
+  The old ``CallSpec2`` alias remains available for now and will be removed in pytest 10.
+
+
+- `#14755 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14755>`_: Schedule *yield_fixture* decorator for removal in pytest 10.
+
+
+- `#14774 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14774>`_: Similarly to the deprecation of class-scoped fixtures defined as instance methods in pytest 9.1,
+  *all* higher-scoped fixtures (``module``, ``package``, and ``session``) defined
+  as instance methods are now deprecated.
+
+  They suffer from the same issue the original deprecation only fixed for
+  class-scoped fixtures, see :issue:`10819` and :issue:`14011`.
+
+
+- `#14808 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14808>`_: Passing a non-string value to a ``string``-typed ini option now emits a ``pytest.PytestRemovedIn10Warning``. This affects ``[tool.pytest.ini_options]`` in ``pyproject.toml``, where TOML arrays are kept as lists by ``make_scalar`` instead of being converted to strings. In pytest 10 this will raise a ``TypeError``, matching the behavior of the corresponding TOML config path.
+
+
+- `#7323 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/7323>`_: Passing ``bytes`` to ``TerminalReporter.write_line()`` is now deprecated, pass a ``str`` instead.
+
+
+
+New features
+------------
+
+- `#14743 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14743>`_: `Full diff:` now contains a legend explaining the `+` & `-` symbols in diff output.
+
+
+- `#2781 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/2781>`_: When :confval:`strict_markers` is enabled, marker names used in :option:`-m` expressions are now validated against registered markers.
+
+
+- `#6881 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/6881>`_: Added a ``parametrize_long_str_id_strategy`` ini option to control how long ``str``/``bytes`` parameter values are handled in auto-generated test IDs. Explicit IDs set via ``ids=[...]`` or ``pytest.param(..., id=...)`` are not affected. Available strategies: ``short`` (default, values over 100 chars fall back to ``argname+index``), ``sha256`` (SHA-256 hex digest), ``legacy`` (keep full value), and ``disallow`` (error requesting explicit IDs).
+
+
+
+Improvements in existing functionality
+--------------------------------------
+
+- `#10745 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/10745>`_: A ``RecursionError`` whose recursion origin cannot be located now shows only the
+  first and last 10 stack frames, matching what pytest already did when locating
+  the origin failed outright. Previously the full traceback -- often around a
+  thousand near-identical frames -- was rendered, which was both slow and
+  unreadable. Pass ``--full-trace`` to see every frame.
+
+
+- `#10745 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/10745>`_: The line numbers of a module's statements are now computed once per traceback
+  instead of once per traceback entry, which noticeably speeds up rendering
+  failures raised from large test modules.
+
+
+- `#11418 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/11418>`_: The cached rewritten modules in ``__pycache__`` are now invalidated by a hash of
+  the source instead of its modification time, using the checked-hash pyc format
+  from :pep:`552`.
+
+  Timestamps make the cache useless wherever source files get fresh modification
+  times, most notably in CI: a checkout gives every file a new mtime, so a
+  restored cache is discarded in full and every test module is rewritten again.
+  Hashing the source costs roughly 15 microseconds per file and makes the cache
+  survive that.
+
+  Existing timestamp based caches are ignored and rewritten once.
+
+
+- `#12624 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12624>`_: The :globalvar:`pytest_plugins` variable and the :envvar:`PYTEST_PLUGINS` environment variable now also accept entry point names of installed plugins (e.g. ``xdist``), in addition to importable module names, matching the behavior of the :option:`-p` command-line option.
+
+  As part of this change, plugins specified by entry point name through these mechanisms are now also listed in the ``plugins:`` line of the terminal header (:issue:`12615`).
+
+  Based on the original implementation by Marcel Telka in :pr:`12616`.
+
+
+- `#12697 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12697>`_: Warnings emitted while importing plugins through :option:`-p`, :envvar:`PYTEST_PLUGINS`, or entry point autoloading are now captured, filtered, and reported like other warnings.
+
+
+- `#12860 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12860>`_: Assertion diffs for ``dict.items()`` and ``dict.keys()`` comparisons (``>=``, ``<=``, ``>``, ``<``, ``==``) now show which items are missing, the same way set comparisons do.
+
+
+- `#13354 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13354>`_: :meth:`Node.get_closest_marker <_pytest.nodes.Node.get_closest_marker>` now also accepts a :class:`~pytest.MarkDecorator` as its ``default``, for example ``item.get_closest_marker("foo", pytest.mark.foo(1))``, and returns the wrapped :class:`~pytest.Mark`.
+
+  Previously the only way to build a ``default`` was to instantiate :class:`~pytest.Mark` directly, which is private and warns.
+
+
+- `#13369 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13369>`_: Improved the error from :meth:`pytest.RunResult.assert_outcomes` when a plugin changes or removes pytest's standard terminal summary, and documented how to isolate output-changing plugins.
+
+
+- `#13431 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13431>`_: Exposed :class:`pytest.ParameterSet` as the type of the return value of :func:`pytest.param()`.
+  This can be used in type annotations and ``isinstance`` checks.
+
+
+- `#13564 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13564>`_: Issue a warning when fixtures are wrapped with a decorator that prevents
+  correct discovery, including ``@classmethod`` above ``@pytest.fixture`` and
+  ``@staticmethod`` above ``@pytest.fixture``. Put ``@pytest.fixture`` above
+  those decorators on test classes.
+
+
+- `#14164 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14164>`_: Exposed :class:`pytest.Approx` as the type of the return value of :func:`pytest.approx()`.
+  This can be used in type annotations and ``isinstance`` checks.
+
+
+- `#14463 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14463>`_: Assertion diffs for mappings now match up keys the way the compared mappings match them themselves.
+
+  Key comparison goes through the mappings' key views instead of plain sets of their keys, so a mapping
+  with its own notion of key equivalence -- case-insensitive header mappings, for example -- no longer
+  reports its common keys as missing on either side.
+
+
+- `#14523 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14523>`_: Large assertion comparison diffs are now built lazily and capped to the
+  truncation budget, so a huge diff is no longer formatted in full just to
+  be truncated. As a result the truncation footer no longer
+  reports the exact number of hidden lines.
+
+
+- `#14687 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14687>`_: The default fd-level output capturing (``--capture=fd``) now skips reading the capture buffer for tests which produce no output, reducing per-test overhead in large test suites.
+
+
+- `#14724 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14724>`_: ``--no-summary`` now only applies directly to pytest's own summary.
+
+  The flag no longer skips the ``pytest_terminal_summary`` hook, so third-party
+  plugins (for example coverage) can still write their terminal summaries.
+
+
+- `#14751 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14751>`_: :func:`parser.addini <pytest.Parser.addini>` now also accepts type expressions for its ``type`` argument, in addition to the existing string tags: the plain Python types ``str``, ``bool``, ``int``, ``float``, a ``Literal`` of strings, and unions of these (for example ``int | str`` or ``int | Literal["auto"]``).
+
+
+- `#14754 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14754>`_: ``pytest.approx()`` now rejects infinite relative tolerances for ``datetime.timedelta`` values with a clear ``ValueError`` instead of raising ``OverflowError``.
+
+
+- `#14791 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14791>`_: The :confval:`junit_family`, :confval:`junit_logging`, :confval:`junit_duration_report`, :confval:`console_output_style`, :confval:`empty_parameter_set_mark`, :confval:`assertion_text_diff_style` and :confval:`tmp_path_retention_policy` configuration options are now registered with the set of values they accept: an invalid value now fails with a clean usage error instead of being silently ignored or crashing later, and ``pytest --help`` lists the accepted values.
+
+  :func:`config.getini <pytest.Config.getini>` now raises :class:`pytest.UsageError` instead of ``TypeError`` or ``ValueError`` when the value read from the configuration file does not match the registered type, so a bad value is always reported as a short usage error message instead of an internal error traceback. Asking for an option name that was never registered still raises ``ValueError``.
+
+
+- `#15006 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/15006>`_: :func:`pytest.approx` now emits :class:`pytest.PytestApproxDecimalToleranceWarning` when a ``rel`` or ``abs`` tolerance is given as a :class:`float` that cannot be represented exactly for a :class:`~decimal.Decimal` comparison, since such a tolerance is widened to the float's exact binary value.
+
+
+- `#15153 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/15153>`_: The :confval:`verbosity_assertions`, :confval:`verbosity_test_cases`, :confval:`verbosity_subtests`, :confval:`tmp_path_retention_count`, :confval:`log_level`, :confval:`log_cli_level`, :confval:`log_file_level` and :confval:`log_auto_indent` configuration options now accept native integer (and, for ``log_auto_indent``, boolean) values in TOML configuration files, while still accepting strings for backward compatibility.
+  :confval:`log_file_mode` and :confval:`parametrize_long_str_id_strategy` now report invalid values as a usage error.
+
+
+- `#15254 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/15254>`_: :fixture:`tmp_path` and :meth:`TempPathFactory.mktemp <pytest.TempPathFactory.mktemp>` no longer list the whole base temporary directory on every call, which made sessions with many temporary directories quadratically slow. Numbers are now handed out from a per-prefix counter, skipping names that already exist.
+
+
+- `#4569 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/4569>`_: :meth:`Node.add_marker <_pytest.nodes.Node.add_marker>` now stores a :class:`~pytest.Mark` in ``node.keywords``, matching what marks applied during collection store. Previously it stored a :class:`~pytest.MarkDecorator`.
+
+
+- `#9436 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/9436>`_: Avoided formatting tracebacks for tests marked with ``xfail(run=False)``.
+
+
+
+Bug fixes
+---------
+
+- `#10128 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/10128>`_: Configured warning filters now apply to warnings emitted by ``pytest_configure`` hooks.
+
+
+- `#10210 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/10210>`_: :func:`pytest.approx` now raises a ``TypeError`` for any nested container, not
+  only for one of the same type as its parent. Previously ``approx([{"k": 1}])``
+  and ``approx({"k": [1]})`` were accepted and then compared unequal to every
+  value, silently ignoring the tolerance, while ``approx([[1]])`` correctly
+  reported that nesting is unsupported.
+
+
+- `#10644 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/10644>`_: ``monkeypatch.setattr()`` no longer leaves a new entry in the instance ``__dict__`` when it patches an attribute that the instance inherits from its class.
+
+  Previously ``undo()`` assigned the inherited value onto the instance, which shadowed the class attribute -- permanently freezing the result for descriptors that resolve dynamically.
+
+
+- `#1139 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/1139>`_: Fixed tracebacks showing ``???`` instead of source lines for code compiled with a filename relative to a directory other than the current working directory -- e.g. compiled Cython modules, when running pytest from a subdirectory of the project root.
+  The source lookup now falls back to searching ``sys.path`` for such filenames, as the standard :mod:`traceback` module does.
+
+
+- `#11502 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/11502>`_: The ``rootdir`` is no longer derived from a configuration file that is not a regular file, such as ``--config-file=/dev/null``.
+
+
+- `#11783 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/11783>`_: Plugins installed in editable mode (:pep:`660`) are marked for assertion rewriting again.
+
+  Such installs do not record the package's Python files in the distribution metadata, so pytest found nothing to rewrite and assertions inside the plugin lost their introspection. The plugin's entry point is now used to locate the package in that case.
+
+
+- `#11933 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/11933>`_: :func:`pytest.warns` no longer re-emits unmatched warnings with ``module="warnings"``, which caused ``module``-based warning filters to be applied to the wrong warnings. Since :class:`warnings.WarningMessage` does not record the module a warning was emitted with, re-emitted warnings now use the standard :func:`warnings.warn_explicit` default of deriving the module from the warning's filename.
+
+
+- `#12175 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12175>`_: :meth:`ExceptionInfo.exconly(tryshort=True) <pytest.ExceptionInfo.exconly>` now strips the ``AssertionError:`` prefix of failed ``assert`` statements for :class:`~pytest.ExceptionInfo` objects created by :func:`pytest.raises`, and failures inside :meth:`unittest.TestCase.subTest` report the same short crash line as regular tests.

+
+
+- `#12824 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12824>`_: Custom command-line options now fail with a clear error when their implicit
+  destination conflicts with an existing option, avoiding silent overrides of
+  built-in options such as ``-k``.

+- `#13292 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13292>`_: Fixed a stale rewritten module being used when a test file is modified twice
+  within the same second without changing its size -- the pyc header could only
+  record whole-second timestamps. The cache is now keyed on a hash of the source.
+
+
+- `#14036 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14036>`_: ``__tracebackhide__`` is now respected in ``ExceptionGroup`` tracebacks, both for the group itself and for its sub-exceptions.
+
+

+
+
+- `#14412 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14412>`_: Fixed incorrect timing information for subtests and parent tests when ``console_output_style="times"``.
+
+
+- `#14445 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14445>`_: Assertion rewriting no longer evaluates walrus operator (``:=``) expressions more than once, which reported results the test never computed when the expression had side effects.

+- `#14635 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14635>`_: Fixed fixture resolution failures when specifying multiple test paths on the command line that share common parent directories. Parametrized fixtures defined in a ``conftest.py`` could be silently dropped depending on the order of the specified paths.

+
+
+- `#14683 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14683>`_: Fixed a regression in pytest 9.1 where a conftest.py located in the rootdir was no longer visible to tests and doctests collected from *outside* the rootdir (for example when passing a parent directory of the rootdir as a collection argument, or setting ``--rootdir`` to a subdirectory).
+
+  As a result, fixtures defined in such a conftest -- including ``doctest_namespace`` injections -- were not available, causing errors such as ``NameError`` in doctests.

+
+- `#14700 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14700>`_: Fixed an internal error on Python 3.12 when a doctest on a fixture-decorated function was skipped.

+
+- `#14705 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14705>`_: TOML configuration files passed via :option:`-c` now also read their configuration from the ``[pytest]`` table, the one pytest's own configuration files use. The ``[tool.pytest]`` and ``[tool.pytest.ini_options]`` tables such files were previously restricted to keep working; using both styles in one file is an error.

+- `#14864 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14864>`_: Fixed collection on Windows collecting the whole suite instead of the given path, on file systems which do not support file IDs (``st_ino`` is ``0`` for every file, as seen for example on ``sshfs-win``/WinFsp mounts).

+- `#14884 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14884>`_: ``Cache.get()``, ``Cache.set()`` and ``Cache.mkdir()`` now reject keys that resolve outside the cache directory, and ``--cache-show`` ignores glob matches outside it.
+
+
+- `#14909 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14909>`_: Fixed :meth:`MonkeyPatch.delattr <pytest.MonkeyPatch.delattr>`, :meth:`MonkeyPatch.setitem <pytest.MonkeyPatch.setitem>` and :meth:`MonkeyPatch.delitem <pytest.MonkeyPatch.delitem>` recording a stale undo entry when the underlying mutation failed, which could cause spurious errors during teardown. The undo entry is now recorded only after the mutation succeeds, matching the behavior of :meth:`MonkeyPatch.setattr <pytest.MonkeyPatch.setattr>`.
+
+
+- `#14912 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14912>`_: :class:`~pytest.PytestWarning` instances defined in ``_pytest.deprecated`` are no longer reused across ``warnings.warn`` calls, so warnings raised as errors (e.g. with ``-W error``) no longer accumulate stale traceback frames from previous raises.
+
+
+- `#14942 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14942>`_: Fixed a regression in 9.1.0 that made collection very slow (quadratic) when many fixtures are defined with the same name.
+  This can happen particularly when many tests are defined in separate classes which inherit from a base class which defines fixtures (the fixtures are repeated per class).
+
+
+- `#14953 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14953>`_: The :confval:`max_warnings` configuration option now accepts integer values in TOML configuration files, while still accepting strings for backward compatibility.
+
+
+- `#15005 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/15005>`_: :func:`pytest.approx` no longer treats finite :class:`~decimal.Decimal` values outside the :class:`float` range (such as ``Decimal("1e400")``) as infinite, which made in-tolerance comparisons fail.
+
+
+- `#15006 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/15006>`_: Restored the tolerance shown by :func:`pytest.approx` for :class:`~decimal.Decimal` values, which since 9.0 displayed ``???`` for the default tolerance and reported the raw ``rel`` ratio instead of the absolute tolerance actually compared against.
+
+
+- `#15006 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/15006>`_: The failure message for :func:`pytest.approx` comparisons of :class:`~decimal.Decimal` collections no longer reports ``Max absolute difference: -inf``, or crashes for mappings, when the :class:`decimal.FloatOperation` trap is set.
+
+
+- `#15006 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/15006>`_: :func:`pytest.approx` no longer raises ``AttributeError`` when comparing :class:`numpy.ndarray` instances with ``object`` dtype, such as arrays of :class:`~decimal.Decimal`.
+
+
+- `#15032 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/15032>`_: Help texts for command-line options and ini options now keep their indentation
+  and blank lines. Previously each line was stripped before wrapping, so a wrapped
+  list item was indistinguishable from a new one and blank lines were dropped; ini
+  option help lost its line breaks entirely.
+
+
+- `#15043 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/15043>`_: Cache writes now emit :class:`pytest.PytestCacheWarning` when writing or closing the cache file fails, consistent with errors opening the file.
+
+
+- `#15052 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/15052>`_: Fixed possible off-by-one line numbers in :option:`--fixtures` and :option:`--fixtures-per-test` output.
+
+
+- `#15132 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/15132>`_: Native TOML numeric values are now accepted for the ``faulthandler_timeout``
+  configuration option.
+
+
+- `#15145 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/15145>`_: With :confval:`console_output_style` set to ``times``, durations just below a unit boundary are now shown in the next unit (e.g. ``1.000ms`` instead of ``1000.0us``).
+
+
+- `#15172 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/15172>`_: Assertion diffs now pretty-print the built-in :class:`frozendict` (Python 3.15+) across multiple lines, similarly to how :class:`dict` is displayed.
+
+
+- `#4569 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/4569>`_: :option:`-k` no longer matches attributes that end up in a test function's ``__dict__`` without being meant as keywords, such as pytest's own ``pytestmark`` attribute and the bookkeeping left behind by :func:`functools.wraps` and :func:`functools.lru_cache`.
+
+
+- `#6750 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/6750>`_: Fix fixture argument discovery for custom collectors that pass bound methods to :class:`pytest.Function`.
+
+
+- `#6997 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/6997>`_: XFAIL reports from teardown phases now include the phase in the short test
+  summary.
+
+
+- `#7940 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/7940>`_: Fixed cleanup of temporary directories failing when subdirectories have their execute permission removed.
+
+
+- `#8321 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/8321>`_: Fixed exception chains being duplicated in the traceback output when an exception in the chain (``__cause__``/``__context__``) has no traceback of its own, and that exception is itself linked to further exceptions.
+
+
+- `#8914 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/8914>`_: Tests parametrized with higher-than-function scope are now reordered by
+  parameter *value* rather than by parameter *index*, so that items using equal
+  parameter values are grouped together and share a single fixture setup, even
+  when they are parametrized by separate :ref:`@pytest.mark.parametrize <pytest.mark.parametrize ref>`
+  calls. Previously, an expensive higher-scoped fixture could be set up and torn
+  down repeatedly for the same parameter value.
+
+  Unhashable parameter values (e.g. dicts) keep the previous index-based
+  grouping behavior.
+
+  As a consequence, the order in which parametrized tests run may change
+  (fixture setup/teardown counts can only decrease, not increase).
+
+
+- `#9924 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/9924>`_: Fixed doctest option flags leaking between docstrings after a failure, skip, or expected failure.
+
+
+
+Improved documentation
+----------------------
+
+- `#10721 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/10721>`_: Replaced ``setup.py`` usage with ``pyproject.toml`` in :ref:`writing-plugins`.
+
+
+- `#12658 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12658>`_: Moved the fixture setup and finalizer hooks to the test running hooks section in the reference documentation.
+
+
+- `#12857 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12857>`_: Documented how ``--confcutdir`` affects initial ``conftest.py`` discovery.
+
+
+- `#14157 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14157>`_: Added the ``pytest-flakefighters`` plugin to the list of flaky test plugins in ``plugins.rst``.
+  Added flaky test papers published on the `Test FLARE <https://test-flare.github.io/>`__ project to the list of flaky papers in ``plugins.rst``.
+
+
+- `#14834 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14834>`_: Added :pypi:`pytest-skip-slow` to the annotated list of third-party plugins.

title: build(deps): Bump the github-actions group with 3 updates
body:
Bumps the github-actions group with 3 updates: [hynek/build-and-inspect-python-package](https://github.com/hynek/build-and-inspect-python-package), [pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish](https://github.com/pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish) and [actions/setup-python](https://github.com/actions/setup-python). Updates `hynek/build-and-inspect-python-package` from 3.0.1 to 3.0.2
Release notes

Sourced from hynek/build-and-inspect-python-package's releases.

v3.0.2

This is a pure security dependency update brought to you by the number 4.

Changelog

Sourced from hynek/build-and-inspect-python-package's changelog.

Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on Keep a Changelog, and this project adheres to Semantic Versioning.

Unreleased

3.0.2 - 2026-10-21

  • Bump certifi to 2026.10.19 to address GHSA-6q48-6c7w-9gw2. #248

3.0.1 - 2026-07-30

Fixed

  • To avoid uv configuration interference with the project that is being built, the installation of our own tools is now ran in a different directory. Additionally, UV_EXCLUDE_NEWER is unset. #240

3.0.0 - 2026-07-30

Security

  • Given the increase and supply-chain attacks and advancements in tooling (for example, pinact or GitHub's Dependabot), this action will stop force-tagging minor and micro releases. This means, there will be no @v3 or @v3.0 tag that gets updated and force-pushed with each update. Always tag with the full version and commit hash; use Zizmor to secure your actions if you can.

Changed
